newsitem.title: USA: Ohio Casualty Q2 property premiums up.
newsitem.headline: Ohio Casualty Q2 property premiums up.

text.p: Ohio Casualty Corp said property-casualty net written premiums rose 2.5 percent to $318.2 million in the second quarter.
Operating income in the second quarter rose to $0.80 a share from $0.09 a share a year ago. The First Call consensus estimate was $0.77 a share.
The combined ratio, a key measure of underwriting profitablity, was 101.7 percent in the second quarter, down from 113.8 percent a year ago, Ohio Casualty said.
An underwriting profit occurs when the combined ratio falls below 100 percent.

Catastrophe losses in the quarter were $4.6 million, down from $19.7 million in the 1996 second quarter. Second quarter catastrophe losses contributed 1.5 points to the combined ratio in 1997 and 6.4 points in 1996.
Ohio Casualty Corporation is the parent organization of several insurance companies that offer businesses and individuals a range of property-casualty and premium financing products.
